vocab.en: What do you like to do?
vocab.tip: The question to ask someone about their hobbies.

vocab.trick: Adore is the same as English: j'adore = I adore, I love.
Think “horror”: I have horror of it. J'ai horreur de faire les courses!

vocab.tip: J'aime + a person can also mean “I love”: j'aime mon frère.

vocab.trick: Mieux means “better”: j'aime mieux = I like better = I prefer.
Aller = to go. Au = à + le: “to the”.
Plage sounds like “plaj”, like a beach in Persian too: پلاژ.
Montagne looks like “mountain”.
Chanter = to chant, to sing. Douche = shower, like دوش.
Conduire = to conduct a car. Voiture sounds like “vehicle”.
Cuisine = the kitchen and the food; cuisiner = to make cuisine.

vocab.tip: Your book spells it diner; dîner with a hat is the older spelling. Both are correct.

vocab.trick: Dormir: a dormitory is where you sleep. Tard = late, like “tardy”.
Faire = to do. French says “do camping, do skiing”: faire du camping, faire du ski.
Les courses = the errands you run around for, like running a course.
Fête = party, feast (the hat hides the s of feast).
A promenade is a walk along the water in English too.
Jouer à + a game. À + les = aux: jouer aux cartes.
Foot = football = soccer. À + le = au: jouer au foot.
Jeu = game, jeux = games. Jouer and jeu come from the same word: play.
Journal = newspaper (a daily: jour = day).
Piscine sounds like پیسین. Nager: think “natation”, swimming.
Parler = to talk: a parliament is where people talk.
Soir = evening, so a soirée is an evening party. Ensemble = together.
Regarder = to look at, to watch (think “regard”).
Rester = to stay, to rest. Maison = house.
Rigoler sounds like “giggle”.
Sortir = to go out. A sortie is a way out.
Jardin = garden. Travailler = to work (think “travail”, hard work).
Voyager = to go on a voyage.

grammars.title: Aimer + infinitive

teach.title: Aimer: to like, to love
teach.body: Use aimer to say you like or love something or someone. Its form changes with the subject, like être and avoir.

examples.fr: Est-ce que tu aimes ton cours d'informatique ?
examples.en: Do you like your computer science class?
examples.pr: ESS-kuh tü EM tohn koor dan-for-mah-TEEK
examples.fa: اِس‌کُ تو اِم تُن کور دَنفُرماتیک

teach.title: The -er pattern
teach.body: Aimer is a regular -er verb. Drop -er and add -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Most French verbs work this way. The forms in the L-shape (j'aime, tu aimes, il aime, ils aiment) all sound the same: “em”. The endings -es and -ent are silent!
teach.trick: Only nous and vous sound different. Everything else is just “em”: j'aime, tu aimes, il aime, ils aiment.

teach.title: Aimer + infinitive
teach.body: To say what someone likes to do, put the infinitive right after aimer. To say what someone doesn't like, wrap ne … pas around aimer: ne becomes n' before a vowel.

examples.en: I like to eat dinner in a restaurant.

examples.fr: Mes amis aiment jouer au football.
examples.en: My friends like to play soccer.

teach.trick: Ne … pas is a sandwich: the conjugated verb is the filling. Je n'aime pas danser.

teach.title: Détester and adorer
teach.body: Détester (to hate) and adorer (to love) follow the same pattern as aimer, and can also take an infinitive.

examples.fr: Je déteste étudier le samedi soir.
examples.en: I hate to study on Saturday nights.
examples.pr: zhuh day-TEST ay-tü-DYAY luh sahm-DEE SWAR
examples.fa: ژُ دِتِست اِتودیه لُ سامدی سوآر

examples.fr: J'adore dormir tard le dimanche matin.
examples.en: I love to sleep late on Sunday mornings.
examples.pr: zhah-DOR dor-MEER TAR luh dee-MAHNSH mah-TAN
examples.fa: ژادُر دُرمیر تار لُ دیمانش ماتَن

notes: aimer: j'aime, tu aimes, il/elle/on aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils/elles aiment.
aimer + infinitive: J'aime danser. Negative: Je n'aime pas danser.
Détester and adorer work the same way: Je déteste étudier. J'adore voyager.

grammars.title: Dates, age and numbers beyond 100

teach.title: La date
teach.body: In French, the day comes before the month, and you use plain numbers: le vingt avril. The only exception is the 1st: le premier. Months are not capitalized. 25.12.20 = le 25 décembre 2020.

examples.fr: Aujourd'hui, nous sommes le premier janvier.
examples.pr: oh-zhoor-DWEE, noo SUM luh pruh-MYAY zhahn-VYAY
examples.fa: اُژوردویی، نو سُم لُ پرُمیه ژانویه

teach.trick: Only the 1st is special: le premier. Every other day is just the number: le deux, le trois, le trente et un.

teach.sub: The months. Tap each one to hear it.

teach.title: Your age: avoir + ans
teach.body: In French you have your years: j'ai vingt ans = I am twenty. Use avoir (to have) + number + ans. Never “je suis vingt”.
teach.trick: Ans means years: j'ai 20 ans = I have 20 years. Ans always links: vingt_ans, huit_ans.

teach.title: Your birthday
teach.body: To give your birthday, use Mon anniversaire est le …. To say the year you were born, use Je suis né en … (add an e if you're a woman: née; it sounds the same).

examples.fr: Mon anniversaire est le vingt et un septembre.
Je suis née en deux mille trois.
examples.pr: zhuh swee NAY ahn duh meel TRWAH
examples.fa: ژُ سویی نه آن دُ میل تروا

teach.title: Numbers beyond 100
teach.body: Cent takes an s only when nothing follows: deux cents, but deux cent un. Mille never takes an s: deux mille. Million and milliard do: deux millions. French writes a period in big numbers: 1.000.000. Years before 2000 can be said two ways: 1998 = mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-huit or dix-neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-huit.
teach.trick: Cents loses its s when it isn't last: deux cents, deux cent un. Mille is never plural.

notes: Dates: day before month, plain numbers: le vingt avril. The 1st is le premier.
Months are lowercase: janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre.
Age: avoir + number + ans: J'ai vingt ans. Quel âge as-tu ?
avoir: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.
Birthday: Mon anniversaire est le … Born: Je suis né(e) en …
deux cents but deux cent un; mille never takes an s; deux millions, deux milliards.
French uses a period in big numbers: 1.000.000.

options: le vingt-cinq décembre deux mille vingt
le décembre vingt-cinq deux mille vingt
